text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hunger revolt does not stir residents of western Bekaa valley.
Former Hizbollah leader Sheikh Sobhi Tufaili this month launched a "hunger revolt" in the form of a civil disobedience campaign to pressure the government into easing poverty.
- Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri to head to Spain and London today.
- Lebanese Christian Maronite Patriarch Cardinal Nasrallah Sfeir says postponement of local elections hampers democracy.
The Lebanese parliament this month delayed for a second time nationwide local elections originally scheduled for June.
- Government calls on parliament to hold a meeting to discuss a new law organising the country's security forces.
- Official Iraqi newspapers continue attacking Lebanon for preventing Iraqi athletes from taking part in Pan Arab Games in Beirut.
- Lebanon complains about Israeli attacks on civilians in south Lebanon.
- Minister of economy and trade says the deficit is Lebanon's biggest problem.
